newsitem.title: UK: Lasmo H1 profit seen unchanged to higher.
newsitem.headline: Lasmo H1 profit seen unchanged to higher.

text.p: British oil exploration and production company Lasmo Plc is expected to report unchanged to higher profits on Thursday.
Forecasts range for net income before exceptional items between 24 million and 32 million stg compared with 24 million stg a year ago.
Lower taxes will help, while the most upbeat analysts also predict that results will be fuelled by higher production.
Taxes are expected to fall in the absence of a 23 million stg divestment gain which inflated taxable income a year ago.

The one-off gain stemmed from the sale of Lasmo Nova Scotia Ltd early in 1996. Lasmo at the time also suffered from teething problems at the Liverpool Bay field off north-west England, which held back production.
But with the field fully operational now, analyst Peter Hitchens at Williams de Broe sees Lasmo's total production rise to an average over 200,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
This compares with 172,000 for the first half of 1996.
But other industry watchers are less bullish, pointing to development delays at the MacCulloch oil field in the North Sea.
"Production will probably be fairly static," said Jonathan Wright at Merrill Lynch.
Analysts agree that sterling's strength will have cancelled out the positive impact of a higher oil price.
North Sea Brent averaged $19.85 per barrel in the first half of 1997, which was about half a dollar higher than in the same 1996 period.
